title: 3. CLI & Linux Core Terms
content:
# 3. CLI & Linux Core Terms

A shared vocabulary makes documentation, troubleshooting, and command usage much easier.

| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| CLI | Command-line interface | Bash session |
| Terminal | Program that provides terminal I/O | GNOME Terminal, iTerm2 |
| Shell | Command interpreter | Bash, Zsh |
| Command | A built-in, executable, function, or alias invoked by name | `ls` |
| Argument | Input supplied to a command | `file.txt` |
| Option/flag | Changes command behavior | `ls -l` |
| Path | Location in the filesystem namespace | `/var/log/app.log` |
| Process | Running instance of a program | PID 1234 |
| PID | Process identifier | `1234` |
| File descriptor | Integer handle for an open I/O stream | `1` = stdout |
| Environment variable | Name/value passed through a process environment | `PATH` |
| stdin/stdout/stderr | Conventional input/output/error streams | FDs 0/1/2 |
| Root | Superuser account with broad privileges | UID 0 |
| Distribution | Packaged Linux operating system | Debian, Fedora |
| Package | Installable software artifact | `.deb`, `.rpm` |
| Daemon/service | Background process providing a function | `sshd` |
| Socket | Kernel-managed communication endpoint | TCP listening socket |
| Mount | Attaches a filesystem into the directory tree | `/mnt/data` |

## Anatomy of a command

```bash
grep -n "ERROR" app.log
```

- command: `grep`
- option: `-n`
- pattern argument: `ERROR`
- input file argument: `app.log`

Not every option is a simple boolean. Some options consume values:

```bash
head -n 20 app.log
```

## Discover before guessing

```bash
type cd
command -v grep
grep --help
man grep
```

For shell built-ins, use:

```bash
help cd
```

## Exit status

Do not assume every non-zero status means the same thing. Programs define their own status meanings.

For example, search tools may use one non-zero status to mean "no match" rather than "fatal error."

## Root and sudo

`root` is UID 0. `sudo` allows an authorized user to execute a command with elevated privileges.

Prefer:

```bash
sudo systemctl restart nginx
```

over starting a permanent root shell when you only need one privileged action.

## Practice

Pick five commands and identify:

1. what executable or built-in implements them;
2. which options they accept;
3. what arguments they expect;
4. what their exit status means;
5. whether they require elevated privileges.
